about: Explicit census decisions where the rules in fmdb/address_census.py cannot tell an address from a coincidence. 'C': leave the literal as written. 'A': an address; 'method' names a resolution the resolver must use ('range': a range bound, kept at the same offset inside the same section; 'page': the page of another address in the same file; 'manual': never resolved mechanically, so the code refuses on another build). 'of' (with 'page'): the page of that one address. Keys are files relative to fm_live_mcp/, or '*' for every file; keys starting adviser/ are pi-fm's tactic writer, relative to the repository root (its census: fmdb/data/adviser_census.json.gz). Reviewed by hand on 12 November 2026 against build 27.0.0.2493426.

builds_about: Per build (plugin sha256), read by fmdb/address_map.py: 'values' are addresses established by hand from both builds' code (they replace what the automatic methods found); 'guards' are native guards whose code changed but whose meaning for the decoder was established by comparing both builds' code, re-derived from the new bytes at 'new' (and 'length' when the span's length changed) only when the address map puts the span there. Verdicts: 'registers' the same instructions up to register allocation, stack slots or instruction order; 'shape' the same fields and values reached through different code; 'ported' the logic changed and the reader's port follows the new build (the evidence names the change and the code that follows it). Each entry carries its evidence: the instructions on both builds. 'adviser_guards' are the same kind of review for pi-fm's tactic writer (fmdb/adviser_update.py), keyed by adviser/pi/<file>; their verdicts: 'same' (the same logic up to registers, instruction order or a hoisted constant), 'context flag' (the same logic except a context word the caller passes), 'behaviour equal on the tested inputs' (changed code whose results were compared on both builds by scripts/adviser_two_build.py and found equal).
